correctness.rationale: For four independent Haar points, the minimizing displacements U,V are independent uniform vectors in the centered lattice Voronoi cell and the relative start point is Haar. Two different crossing parameters would give two distinct representatives of the same torus point inside the Voronoi fundamental cell because (s-s')U and (t-t')V lie in its interior for differences in (-1,1), contradicting uniqueness. Therefore the random arcs have at most one transverse crossing and p=E|det(U,V)|/area(V). In reduced coordinates (B=a²+b²>=1,q=2a in [0,1]), the cell is a centrally symmetric six-gon H defined by |u|<=1,|v|<=B,|v-u|<=B+1-q. Partition the positive half into four radial triangles with d=(B,B(2-q),q(B+1-q),B-q); triangle self- and cross-determinant integrals yield 54I=5(4B-q²)^3-3q²(2B-q)^2(2-q)^2. I separately expanded/factored this polynomial exactly via symbolic algebra, not by stochastic sampling. Consequently p=5/54-q²(2B-q)²(2-q)²/[18(4B-q²)^3]; logarithmic derivative in B and monotonic deficit at B=1 prove sharp 22/243 (unique hexagonal lattice) and 5/54 (all rectangular), including degenerate reduced-boundary coordinates.

value.rationale: Crossings of two independent minimizing geodesics define a canonical invariant of every flat two-torus. The closed rational moduli-space profile, universal sharp range, and geometrically distinct equality classes give a natural complete extremal classification. The exact Voronoi determinant identity can serve as a reusable structural tool but no further extension is claimed.

limitations: Only two shortest arcs joining four independent area-uniform endpoints on Euclidean flat two-tori, not curved surfaces, non-shortest geodesics, or higher correlations.
Null ties and degenerate crossings excluded almost surely with justified measure-zero argument.
An unindexed equivalent stochastic-geometric formula may exist.
